external_sources: Encore Heureux: „Le Pavillon Circulaire“, official project page, 70 m², 2015, 60 % materials with prior life, 180 wooden doors, mineral wool, timber frame from leftover construction material, exhibition panels, Paris-Plage terrace decking, four public-lighting suspensions, 80,000 € HT. https://encoreheureux.org/en/projects/pavillon-circulaire

designboom: „encore heureux uses reused materials to build circular pavilion“, 2015, 180 wooden doors, materials from construction sites/unused stock, 70 m², COP21 context. https://www.designboom.com/architecture/encore-heureux-architects-circular-pavilion-paris-12-16-2015/
e-architect: „The Circular Pavilion Paris“, about 60 % materials with second life; 180 doors from Paris 19th housing rehabilitation. https://www.e-architect.com/paris/the-circular-pavilion-in-paris

Architect Magazine: „The Reclaimed Circular Pavilion“, 2016, describes 80 % building components in second/third life; note as conflicting with official 60 %. https://www.architectmagazine.com/technology/architectural-detail/the-reclaimed-circular-pavilion_o

Trä magazine / Swedish Wood: „Opening door to recycling“, 180 oak doors, insulation from convenience-store roof, timber frame leftover from old people’s home, relocation to sports club. https://www.swedishwood.com/publications/wood-magazine/2016-2/opening-door-to-recycling/
